prompt:
Harbor Dispatch is standardizing its configuration vocabulary. Replace the public configuration key `deliveryChannel` with `channel` throughout the application, tenant configuration, CLI, checked-in JSON, operational scripts, visible tests and documentation. This is a clean migration: no compatibility alias, legacy property access, legacy object field or legacy CLI flag may remain in src/, scripts/ or config/. Update the README and changelog. Textual cleanup is required too: do not leave the literal names deliveryChannel, HARBOR_DELIVERY_CHANNEL or --delivery-channel anywhere in src/, scripts/, config/ or README.md, including comments or migration notes; historical notes may go in the changelog instead.

The only accepted channels remain email, sms and webhook. Defaults are email, batchSize 25, sender harbor. Environment input must use HARBOR_CHANNEL (not HARBOR_DELIVERY_CHANNEL), and the CLI must accept --channel (not --delivery-channel). Unsupported flags must fail. loadConfig accepts exactly channel, batchSize and sender, rejects any other key with `unsupported config key: <key>`, and preserves the documented validation errors. Passing deliveryChannel must therefore fail, even when channel is also present. tenantConfig must reject unknown tenant override keys too. All configuration consumers, routing, rendering, planning, retry policy, receipts, metrics and serialization must work with channel alone, including SMS's 160-character limit and webhook JSON payloads. Configuration persistence writes only the canonical fields; do not add fallback reads. Keep existing output ordering and domain behavior.

Use Node 22 built-in TypeScript stripping; no dependencies or compilation. Run visible tests with `node --test tests/*.test.ts`; exercise CLI with `node scripts/dispatch.ts --channel sms --message hello`. README documents the complete public contracts and output shapes.
